User.title: User
User.description: Represents a platform owner or administrator of the 'Platformify Bookings' system, managing access rights and owned white-label platforms.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

email.description: The email address of the user.

role.description: The role of the user within the platform (e.g., 'platform_owner', 'super_admin').

ownedPlatformIds.description: An array of IDs referencing Platforms owned by this user. (Relationship: User 1:N Platform)

Platform.title: Platform
Platform.description: Represents a single white-label booking marketplace instance created by a platform owner.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Platform entity.

ownerId.description: Reference to the User who owns this platform. (Relationship: User 1:N Platform)

name.description: The display name of the white-label booking platform (e.g., 'Indonesian Event Venues').

customDomain.description: The custom domain configured for the white-label platform.

themeConfig.description: A JSON string containing configuration settings for the platform's theme, including colors, logos, and UI.

status.description: The current operational status of the platform (e.g., 'active', 'suspended').

Listing.title: Listing
Listing.description: Represents an item or service available for booking within a specific white-label platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Listing entity.

platformId.description: Reference to the Platform this listing belongs to. (Relationship: Platform 1:N Listing)

title.description: The title of the listing (e.g., 'Grand Ballroom at Hotel Indah').

description.description: A detailed description of the listing.

pricePerDay.description: The price per day for booking this listing.

availabilityCalendar.description: A list of dates when the listing is available, in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.

Customer.title: Customer
Customer.description: Represents an end-user who makes bookings on a specific white-label platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Customer entity.

platformId.description: Reference to the Platform this customer is associated with. (Relationship: Platform 1:N Customer)

name.description: The full name of the customer.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

bookingIds.description: An array of IDs referencing bookings made by this customer. (Relationship: Customer 1:N Booking)

Booking.title: Booking
Booking.description: Represents a specific booking made by a customer for a listing on a white-label platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Booking entity.

platformId.description: Reference to the Platform this booking belongs to. (Relationship: Platform 1:N Booking)

listingId.description: Reference to the Listing that is being booked. (Relationship: Listing 1:N Booking)

customerId.description: Reference to the Customer who made the booking. (Relationship: Customer 1:N Booking)

startDate.description: The start date and time of the booking.

endDate.description: The end date and time of the booking.

totalPrice.description: The total calculated price for the booking.

status.description: The current status of the booking (e.g., 'pending', 'confirmed', 'completed', 'cancelled').

Dedicated collection for users with 'super_admin' privileges. The existence of a document here grants global administrative access, adhering to the DBAC principle of 'Existence over Content' for authorization. Documents may be minimal (e.g., `{ id: userId }`).

params.description: The Firebase Authentication UID of the super administrator.

firestore.reasoning:
The core of this design prioritizes Authorization Independence and supports Queries as Authorization Primitives (QAPs) through strategic denormalization and structural segregation. This approach ensures robust, debuggable security rules and scalable data access.

**Authorization Independence via Denormalization:**
1.  **Platform Ownership:** The `ownerId` is explicitly stored within each `/platforms/{platformId}` document. This enables security rules to directly verify `request.auth.uid == resource.data.ownerId` for any operation on a platform, eliminating the need for `get()` calls to a parent `User` document.
2.  **Subcollection Ownership:** For all subcollections (`listings`, `customers`, `bookings`) nested under a `Platform`, the `ownerId` of the parent platform is denormalized and copied into every document (e.g., a document in `/platforms/{platformId}/listings/{listingId}` will contain `ownerId`). This is critical for atomic operations and simplifies security rules, allowing the platform owner to manage their resources by checking `request.auth.uid == resource.data.ownerId` directly on the document being accessed. This also ensures that `list` operations can be secured effectively without relying on `get()` calls.
3.  **Customer-Specific Access:** For `Booking` entities, the `customerId` is included within the booking document. This allows individual customers to access their own bookings by verifying `request.auth.uid == resource.data.customerId`, further enhancing authorization independence.

**Structural Segregation for Homogeneous Security Posture:**
1.  **Role-Based Access:** Dedicated top-level collections like `/super_admins/{userId}` and `/platform_owners/{userId}` are used for global role-based authorization. This adheres to the DBAC principle of "Existence over Content", where the presence of a document signifies the role, allowing for efficient `exists()` checks in security rules rather than `get()` calls on a user profile to check a `role` field.
2.  **Tenant Isolation:** Each white-label platform (`/platforms/{platformId}`) serves as a tenant root. Its subcollections (`listings`, `customers`, `bookings`) are designed to share a common security posture primarily managed by the platform's `ownerId`, or, for customer-specific data, by the `customerId`. This simplifies rule definitions by ensuring all documents within a given collection or subcollection follow similar access patterns.

**Queries as Authorization Primitives (QAPs):**
1.  **Secure `list` Operations for Owners:** The denormalization of `ownerId` into `Platform` and its nested entities allows platform owners to securely query for their owned resources using client-side `where` clauses, e.g., `db.collection('platforms').where('ownerId', '==', currentUser.uid)`. Security rules can then enforce that the `ownerId` in the query matches `request.auth.uid`.
2.  **Secure `list` Operations for Customers:** The inclusion of `customerId` in `Booking` documents allows customers to securely list only their own bookings: `db.collection('platforms/{platformId}/bookings').where('customerId', '==', currentUser.uid)`.
3.  **Public Data Access:** Publicly accessible data, such as `listings` for a given white-label platform, can be made available for `read` operations on the `/platforms/{platformId}/listings` collection, with rules ensuring the parent platform is active. This enables client applications (the white-label frontends) to query for listings without needing complex authorization filters on the client side, as security is enforced by the rules.

This architecture results in clear, robust, and easily debuggable security rules, minimal `get()` calls, and efficient data access for various user roles and scenarios.
